name: Sustenance Allowance – Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy 2026
provider: UP Startup Mission, Department of IT & Electronics, Government of Uttar Pradesh
amountText: ₹20,000 a month for up to 2 years (up to ₹4.8 lakh in total), paid quarterly. The earlier 2020 policy paid ₹17,500 a month for 1 year.
duration: Up to 24 months, released quarterly
timeToMoney: Not published. Recognition takes about 3 working days; the allowance then depends on your incubator's recommendation and state approval.
deadline: Rolling, through a recognised incubator
oneLiner: A monthly stipend from the UP government so an idea-stage founder can work on the startup full-time instead of taking a job.
what: The Uttar Pradesh Startup Policy 2026 (approved by the state cabinet in July 2026) pays recognised idea-stage startups ₹20,000 a month for up to two years, released every quarter. It is meant to cover the founder's basic living and early running costs while moving from idea to prototype. It replaced the 2020 policy's ₹17,500 a month for one year.
who: Your company, LLP or partnership is registered in Uttar Pradesh
You hold DPIIT (Startup India) recognition and StartInUP recognition from the state portal (free; certificate issued within about 3 working days of a complete application)
You work with a UP government-recognised incubator, which processes and monitors the incentive
You are at the ideation-to-prototype stage (no finished product in the market yet)
notFor: Startups registered outside Uttar Pradesh
Companies that have already launched and are selling (look at UP seed capital instead)
Founders who are not attached to a UP-recognised incubator
Anyone expecting a lump sum: it is paid in quarterly instalments, not upfront
why: It buys you time: up to 24 months of runway to build without a salary
No equity is taken and nothing has to be repaid
It usually comes bundled with incubation, which opens the door to UP prototype and seed grants later
Being in the state system helps with UP government procurement and events
howItWorks: You first get StartInUP recognition on the state portal, then join a UP-recognised incubator. The incubator recommends idea-stage startups for the allowance and the UP Startup Mission (nodal agency under the IT & Electronics Department) approves it. The money is released quarterly. Under the 2020 policy each incubator could recommend up to 25 startups a year; a cap for the 2026 policy was not published on the pages we could read.

name: Seed Funding for Startups Scheme (Haryana State Startup Policy 2022)
provider: Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Haryana
amountText: Seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh per startup, in 3 tranches (50% / 40% / 10%). Travel is capped at ₹50,000 and market research at ₹50,000 within that.

timeToMoney: Applications received in one quarter are evaluated in the next quarter, so expect at least 3–6 months to sanction
deadline: Apply any time before the scheme ends on 6 Jul 2027; reviewed quarterly
oneLiner: A grant of up to ₹10 lakh from the Haryana government to validate an idea and build a prototype.
what: Notified in the Haryana Gazette on 23 July 2024 under the State Startup Policy 2022, this scheme gives Haryana-based startups up to ₹10 lakh to validate the idea, demonstrate a proof of concept, build a prototype, travel to startup events, and do market research and early marketing. It sets quotas by block category: 100 startups in 'A' blocks, 250 in 'B', 750 in 'C' and 1,000 in 'D' (more for less-developed blocks).

howItWorks: You apply online on the Industries & Commerce Department portal. Officials check documents (you get 10 working days to fix gaps), then you pitch to an Evaluation & Approval Committee chaired by the Director General, Industries & Commerce. The committee scores you out of 100 (need, feasibility, impact, uniqueness, team, revenue model, go-to-market, fund-use plan, presentation) and you need at least 60. Approved amounts come in 3 tranches (50/40/10). You can claim the next tranche after using 80% of the previous one, and it is paid once you show 100% utilisation.
